A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Alignment-Aware Decoding by the same authors. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reformatting and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original alignment benchmark results, reward-model accuracies, and experiments on data scarcity, regularization, beam search and iterative DPO.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds human judgments, OLMo evaluations, comparator experiments and supplementary sensitivity and applicability tests.

M1.justification: AAD still greedily maximizes the DPO/SFT token log-probability ratio over candidates passing the same min-alpha filter. Algorithm 1 documents this existing procedure. The entropy-thresholded beam variant is also retained, moving into the appendix.

E1.justification: The six preference datasets and AlpacaEval remain the demonstrated task coverage. New studies vary models, training or evaluators within that coverage. The Ultrachat-to-Ultrafeedback relabeling does not establish a dataset replacement: v1 already references ultrafeedback_binarized, and the corresponding results are identical.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated contrastive-decoding baselines using external 1B and 3B Llama Instruct references in Table 3, and standard beam search across beam widths in Figure 8. These substantially expand comparisons beyond the retained greedy, Bo2 and EFT baselines. Standard beam search is distinct from the AAD beam variant already studied in v1.

E3.justification: The original training protocol remains, but substantial new evaluation designs appear: OLMo 7B/13B models with GPT-4-turbo judging over 805 prompts; 502 human judgments from 40 raters; full-fine-tuning data scaling over 800 held-out prompts; and PPO training for 20,000 episodes. These are added settings, not evidence that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds alpha sensitivity, standard beam-width comparisons, training-duration sensitivity, data scaling under full fine-tuning, iterative-DPO tests on additional retained datasets, and PPO compatibility tests. These examine previously untested robustness and applicability questions. The earlier entropy-thresholded beam analysis is retained in Appendix A.4.

E5.justification: Figure 3 newly reports means and standard deviations across Skywork, Nectar and Argilla, describing cross-dataset variation rather than seed uncertainty. Table 5 adds Bradley-Terry Elo estimation from human judgments. Neither version specifies repeated-seed counts or significance tests.

E6.justification: The original main tables and full-fine-tuning table retain their numbers, while substantial new outcomes are reported. Human AAD win rates include 58.7% against greedy DPO and 73.5% against Bo2; OLMo AlpacaEval win rates against greedy DPO are 71.5% and 75.2%. New negative findings include second-iteration degradation in Table 9 and Skywork PPO reward 3.02 for AAD versus 10.4 for Bo2 in Table 10. Two qualitative Bo2 responses, previously identical to AAD's, are replaced in the Obi-Wan and Dark Knight examples.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.1 introduces a token-level MDP, an effective regularized reward, soft Bellman relations and a derivation connecting the log ratio to human reward and value differences, substantially extending v1's argument. v2 also corrects the extra denominator logarithm in Equation (5) and the missing logarithm in rDPO. The new Equations (12)–(13), however, have an apparent entropy-sign inconsistency with Equation (11).

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution bullets retain the same central claims: inference-time alignment using an SFT/DPO pair without additional training, improved alignment across models and benchmarks, and useful synthetic preference data. The explicit SFT+DPO qualification in v2's conclusion matches the method's already-stated scope.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands mechanism explanations and applicability limits. It attributes smaller full-fine-tuning gains to internalized preference information, interprets second-iteration failures as favoring one synthetic-data round, and explains mixed PPO results through the absence of the DPO probability-gap structure. It also adds interpretations of filtering sensitivity and training-duration effects.

D1.justification: Core optimizer, DPO and LoRA hyperparameters are retained. v2 adds pseudocode, base-model and SFT-workflow information, matching OLMo checkpoint descriptions, GPU and parallel-execution details, and a named GitHub code location replacing the anonymous link. Some oracle base-model descriptions become less specific.

R1.justification: v2 adds Amulet to related work and references supporting the entropy formulation, OLMo models, Qwen3 and SFT workflow; it also removes the min-p citation and revises dataset/model references. The central positioning among training-time alignment, EFT, contrastive decoding and reward-guided search remains.

P1.justification: Most existing abstract, introduction and explanatory prose is preserved. Changes include localized method and caption rewrites, terminology and grammar corrections, an impact statement, and appendix reorganization that consolidates supplementary results and relocates the beam discussion. The main section sequence remains intact.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column to a two-column conference layout. v2 adds six tables, three figures and an algorithm box, restructures Table 2, expands the BoN plot with Nectar curves, and relocates several existing displays. These are substantial visual and layout changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the central method through human preferences, direct contrastive-decoding comparisons, OLMo evaluations and targeted filtering, training and efficiency studies. These address important gaps in v1's evidence and practical characterization. Reporting PPO failures and iterative-DPO degradation also improves applicability guidance. The new derivation's apparent entropy-sign error and inconsistent descriptions of Iter 1' temper the gains, but do not outweigh the stronger empirical support and clearer boundaries.
